intro: Type or tap a calculation with trig, logs, powers, roots or factorials and get the answer straight away. Your recent calculations stay in a history list so you can look back at them or copy a result.

formula.label: Order of operations
formula.expr: brackets → powers and roots → × and ÷ (left to right) → + and − (left to right)

formula.label: Degrees and radians
formula.expr: radians = degrees × π ÷ 180, so 180° = π rad

howItWorks: You build a calculation the same way you would write it on paper. Use the buttons, or type on your keyboard, for example sin(30), sqrt(16), 2^10, 5! or 200*15%, then press = or Enter. You can leave out the × sign in places like 2π or 3(4+1), and it is still read as multiplication.

The calculator follows the usual order of operations: brackets first, then powers and roots, then multiplication and division, then addition and subtraction. The % sign simply divides the number in front of it by 100. log means log base 10 and ln means the natural log, which uses the number e.

The DEG/RAD switch decides how angles are read by sin, cos and tan, and what unit sin⁻¹, cos⁻¹ and tan⁻¹ give back. It starts on DEG, which is what most school problems use. AC clears everything and ⌫ removes the last thing you typed.

example.title: How high does the ladder reach?
example.problem: A 10 m ladder leans against a wall and makes an angle of 60° with the ground. How far up the wall does it reach?
steps: The ladder is the hypotenuse and the height is the side opposite the 60° angle, so height = 10 × sin(60°).
Check that the angle switch shows DEG, because the angle is in degrees.
Tap 10 × sin(60), or type 10*sin(60) on your keyboard, then press = or Enter.
sin(60°) ≈ 0.8660, so the screen shows about 8.660254.
Round to a sensible accuracy: about 8.66 m.
example.answer: The ladder reaches about 8.66 m up the wall.

mistakes.title: Using the wrong angle mode
mistakes.text: If the switch is on RAD, sin(30) gives about −0.988 instead of 0.5, because 30 is read as 30 radians. If a trig answer looks strange, check DEG or RAD first.

mistakes.title: Treating % like a shop discount
mistakes.text: Here % just means divide by 100, so 200 + 15% gives 200.15, not 230. To add 15% to 200, type 200 + 200 × 15% or 200 × 1.15, which both give 230.

mistakes.title: Leaving out brackets
mistakes.text: 1 ÷ 2 × 4 is worked left to right and gives 2. If you meant one over (2 × 4), type 1 ÷ (2 × 4), which gives 0.125.

mistakes.title: Reading sin⁻¹ as 1 ÷ sin
mistakes.text: sin⁻¹ is the inverse sine: it finds the angle that has a given sine. In DEG mode, sin⁻¹(0.5) = 30°. It is not the same as 1 ÷ sin(0.5).

faqs.q: Why does sin(30) give −0.988 and not 0.5?
faqs.a: The calculator is set to RAD, so it reads 30 as 30 radians. Switch to DEG and sin(30) gives 0.5.

faqs.q: What is the difference between log and ln?
faqs.a: log is base 10, so log(100) = 2 because 10² = 100. ln is base e (about 2.718), so ln(100) ≈ 4.605.

faqs.q: Do I have to type the × sign every time?
faqs.a: No. Writing a number right next to π, e or a bracket is read as multiplication, so 2π and 3(4+1) both work. 3(4+1) gives 15.

faqs.q: How do I find a square root or a power from the keyboard?
faqs.a: Type sqrt(16) for a square root, which gives 4, and use ^ for powers, so 2^10 gives 1024. Press Enter to see the answer.
It is 5 factorial: 5 × 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 120. It counts how many ways you can arrange 5 different things in a row.
